topic: Marina Abramović and Ulay's reunion that ended in a lawsuit, not peace
title: Marina Abramović's Viral Reunion Wasn't Actually A Happy Ending
description: AI-narrated original commentary (not a reused clip) on the real, verified story behind Marina Abramović and Ulay's most famous performance pieces, their 1988 breakup on the Great Wall of China, their viral 2010 MoMA reunion, and the lawsuit that followed it. Sources for the central claims are linked below.

hook_candidates.text: Marina Abramović's viral museum reunion never actually meant peace between them at all.
One artist once let her ex aim a drawn arrow straight at her own heart.
Would you let your ex point a drawn arrow at your chest, on purpose?
In 1988, two lovers said goodbye by walking a thousand miles toward each other.

share_trigger: A viewer sends this to the friend who still believes that viral reunion video meant they made peace for good.
contradicted_belief: Most people assume that famous viral museum reunion meant these two artists finally made peace.
closing_comment: That reunion looked like a happy ending, but the real ending was a lawsuit years later.

sources.note: Confirms Rest Energy: 1980 piece, drawn bow pointed at Abramović's heart, heartbeat mics, ~4 minutes.
MoMA confirms the 1988 Great Wall Walk ended Abramović and Ulay's 12-year partnership.
Confirms Ulay's surprise 2010 MoMA appearance and their emotional on-camera reunion.
Confirms an Amsterdam court ordered Abramović to pay Ulay over 250,000 euros in 2016.
